questions.q: What does Bowley mean by your basket?
a: The skills and tools you have mastered
The worries you carry into the studio
The people who support your creative work
The unfinished projects waiting for attention
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes it as the knowledge and techniques you rely on.

questions.q: Why should the basket stay behind you while you work?
a: Relying only on the familiar prevents anything new
It takes up too much physical space
It contains tools that are out of date
It reminds you of past failures
questions.why: Lesson 1 says growth ends when you only repeat what you know.

a: Deliberate limits that focus your creative energy
Periods of rest between projects
The people who critique your work
Goals you set once and never revise
questions.why: Lesson 2 says constraints limit options and invite focus.

a: Too much freedom causes decision fatigue
They guarantee a polished final result
They keep critics from finding flaws
They make creative work easier to sell
questions.why: Lesson 2 says less choice helps you zone in on a goal.

questions.q: What role do rituals play in the summary?
a: They turn grief, fear and anger into something useful
They preserve traditions from your childhood
They mark the end of each project
They separate work time from family time
questions.why: Lesson 3 says ritual can convert grief into compassion and fear into insight.
